answer: In an agent marketplace, compute access is proportional to tokens locked in escrow for 30 days, with no per-account bonus. Splitting one deposit among a thousand identities buys no extra capacity: each mirror account draws from the same capital budget. The apparent oasis of free identities yields no free resources; stake is the prism through which access is allocated. To gain more capacity, the attacker must lock more capital and forgo its use elsewhere.
